note.text:
Telephone words: to dial (enter the number), to ring, a missed call, a text message (an SMS), voicemail, airtime or credit (money for calls), a SIM card, a charger, the battery, a network (the signal), to top up (add credit).
Shopping words: a customer (the buyer), a shop assistant, the price, a discount (money taken off the price), a bargain (a good price), a receipt (the paper that shows you paid), change (money given back), to order (ask to buy), delivery (bringing goods to you), cash or mobile money, out of stock (none left).
Useful questions: “How much is this phone?” “Do you have a cheaper one?” “Can I pay by mobile money?” “Can I have a receipt, please?”

worked_example.problem: A phone costs {p} francs, with a discount of {d} francs. Tabe pays with a note of {g} francs. Use shopping words to explain what happens.
steps: The discount is taken off the price: {p} − {d} = {p - d} francs.
Tabe pays {g} francs, so he gets change: {g} − {p - d} = {g - p + d} francs.
He asks: “Can I have a receipt, please?” The receipt shows he paid.
worked_example.answer: He pays {p - d} francs, gets {g - p + d} francs change and a receipt.

cards.idea: Telephone words: dial a number, top up your credit, charge the battery.
example: I topped up my credit to call my aunt.
My battery is low: where is the charger?

cards.idea: Shopping words: the price, a discount, change and a receipt.
example: The price was ten thousand, with a discount of one thousand.
The shop assistant gave me my change and a receipt.

cards.idea: Polite shopping questions start with How much, Do you have, Can I.
example: Can I pay by mobile money?

questions.prompt: You are in a phone shop. {X.q} What do you say?

pick.s: I can't call: I have no ___ left.
There is no ___ here, so my phone can't make calls.
The shop gave us a ___ of two thousand francs because we bought three phones.
Sorry, that model is ___; we will have more next week.
e: On discount means cheaper, not finished.
A bargain is a good price.

pick.s: I paid five thousand with a ten-thousand note, so I got five thousand in ___.

questions.prompt: One sentence uses a word wrongly. Which one?

right.text: Keep the receipt in case the phone is faulty.
The customer asked for a discount.

wrong.text: The shop assistant gave me a receipt of five hundred francs back.
wrong.explain: Money given back is change; a receipt is a paper.

wrong.text: I put the charger in my phone to make calls cheaper.
wrong.explain: A charger fills the battery; credit pays for calls.

wrong.text: The phone is out of stock, so I bought two.
wrong.explain: Out of stock means there are none left.
